fields.statement: QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): rhiza change new left untracked entries in the main checkout; rhiza check printed 'warn log .rhiza/log/<cs>/<entry>.json: untracked log entry that no model branch or live run holds' with 'next: rhiza model commit-untracked' per entry (the run also failed only on the stale render, not on the warnings); after commit-untracked and in a live run's linked worktree, rhiza check printed no untracked-entry warning.

QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): with entries of two change sets untracked on main (a failed push left them on no branch), rhiza model commit-untracked printed 'committed 3 entries' and 'committed 1 entries on a model branch', pushed two model/<cs>-<entry> branches to origin and called gh pr create once each; the record branch carried the re-rendered .rhiza/rendered files and rhiza check passed on it. A later orphan was committed and PR'd by one rhiza daemon --once tick.

QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): rhiza daemon --once with one green and one red model PR: the green one was merged with gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit, its branch deleted on origin, and main fast-forwarded with the untracked copies of its entries dropped (git status no longer listed them); the red one stayed open and rhiza inbox showed 'model PR ... has failing checks: ci' for its change set. TestSelfUpdate's self-update path was not exercised by hand.

QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): rhiza health's main part was bad with '4 untracked log entries on no branch' and one line per entry naming entry, change set and rhiza model commit-untracked; once the entries sat on model branches or in a live run's worktree it was ok, listing each as 'pending ... held by a model branch or run'.

QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): with a run of a sleep-40 command workflow live on a change set, rhiza apply --change <cs> in the main checkout wrote the entry there and copied it byte-for-byte into the run's worktree .rhiza/log (untracked there for the run's next commit); no model branch or gh call was made, health listed it as held and rhiza check in either checkout gave no warning. The run's next commit was not exercised by hand.

QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): rhiza change new and rhiza apply --change in the main checkout pushed model/<cs>-<entry> branches from origin/main holding exactly the written entries and opened one PR; a second write to the same change set added a commit to the same branch (gh pr view, no second pr create); no temporary worktree remained in git worktree list.

QA cycle 1, hands-on with rhiza built from this branch (go build into the session scratchpad) in a scratch repo with a local bare origin, real git and a scripted gh standing in for GitHub (pr view/create/merge; merge squash-merges into the bare origin): rhiza run start --foreground --workflow plan --new 'QA plan reports' (and --milestone) opened the run's worktree, wrote the open entry there and committed it on cs/<slug>; rhiza change show worked from main and check/health called the main copy held. But the same run also pushed model/<cs>-<open entry> to origin and called gh pr create for it: the open entry is shipped as a model-only PR too, not only on the run's branch.
